I have an older Gary Fisher hybrid bike (Avant Garde model) and I'm thinking about getting forks with shocks for a possibly smoother ride. I mostly ride on trails that aren't too rugged, so it's not really a necessity but I was just wondering what you guys thought of shock forks.

I have a fatbike with shock forks (overkill, I know) and it's really nice for commuting, especially if your city/town has shit roads. Boston roads are jacked up from the snow plows after last winter so there are lots of nasty hand stinging potholes everywhere.

If you don't want it you can also just lock it and then bike like it was a normal fork.
My first thought is that it would screw with the geometry of your bike, especially if the bike was built without a suspension fork in mind. Maybe just some wider tires?

I have front shocks on one of my mountain bikes. I mainly use that one for road or light off-road biking. I can't go back to a rigid fork. I love the front shocks. I bike the Schuylkill River Trail, which is mostly paved, and after 40 - 50 miles, every little bump hurts. But then again, I'm in my 40's and shit starts to hurt all over for no reason anyway.

Get the widest tires you can fit and run just enough pressure not to pinch flat. You could try tubeless too for even lower pressures. That's going to give you way better small bump absorption than shocks ever could.

Throw my voat against front forks, mainly because it's not really required but also because unless you spend a lot the forks you'll get won't last for longer than a few years and will need regular servicing.
